input.note: The ONNX graph scales its own input. The layers below take scaled input, as `scaling` says.

attribution: Altman et al., 'Realistic Synthetic Financial Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering Models', NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. Data: IBM Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering (AML), CDLA-Sharing-1.0.
modifications: Not the published transaction rows: `fixtures.rows` is 16 rows drawn from the held-out temporal test window, half of them laundering, each one 114 features computed from the transactions by the training script, stored as float32. `fixtures.logits` is what the exported graph gives them.
note: Trained on labels with class weights, on the fit window; threshold tuned on the validation window and folded into the last bias, so argmax over the two logits is the decision. Fixture rows are from the held-out test window, half of them laundering by construction. Features see transactions up to the end of their batch of 2048, at most 17 minutes past the transaction, as the Graph Feature Preprocessor paper processes them.
